answers.children: Yes — English Setters are good with children because their gentle and affectionate nature leads them to play tenderly with kids while instinctively moderating their energetic build around smaller family members. Their medium size and loving temperament make them tolerant playmates that lean in for affection rather than overwhelm, though their boundless energy from bird hunting heritage requires supervision during rough games. The graceful hunter still retains a soft soul that matches well with family life. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 8/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — English Setters generally get along with other pets thanks to their sociable and affectionate temperament, yet their bird-hunting instincts and pointing background can make them overly curious around smaller animals such as cats. Their gentle nature supports peaceful interactions with dogs of both sexes when properly introduced, but the same high energy that drives field work may spark chasing if prey drive is not managed. Owners must channel their stamina into suitable outlets.
answers.exercise: English Setters need 60 to 90 minutes of vigorous daily exercise because they were bred for hours of hunting across rugged terrain and possess exceptional stamina. Without this their boundless energy turns into restlessness that can produce digging and destructive behaviour indoors. Activities that suit their graceful build and pointing heritage include off-leash runs in secure areas, scent games and long hikes that engage both mind and body.
answers.shedding: Yes — English Setters shed moderately year-round with possible seasonal increases; their medium silky coat carries feathering on the tail and legs that traps loose hair and requires regular attention to prevent mats. The graceful hunter’s flowing, speckled coat spreads noticeable hair around the house especially during shedding periods, matching their energetic lifestyle that brings them through fields and home again.
answers.hypoallergenic: The English Setter's medium silky coat sheds moderately and releases dander into the home environment. Its feathering on the tail and legs traps dust and pollen after a day in the field, requiring regular grooming to manage. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic and the English Setter is not among those usually suggested to allergy sufferers. (PawLabs shedding score: 6/10)
answers.training: English Setters are moderately easy to train because their intelligence and sharp ability to learn complex tasks from bird-hunting days combine with affectionate willingness to please family, yet their energetic independence can lead to mischief when bored. The breed’s history of reading subtle cues in the field supports good trainability if owners provide consistent direction that channels their stamina and gentle soul.
answers.lifespan: English Setters live 10-12 years on average. Their medium-sized graceful build and history as working bird dogs support reasonable robustness, though their high energy levels and need for purpose mean that insufficient exercise can affect overall condition. The affectionate hunter’s loving temperament does not alter the typical sporting-dog lifespan range.
answers.size: English Setters reach 45-80 lb and stand 23-27 in tall at the shoulder. Their elegant proportions and feathered build feel substantial yet graceful to live with, offering a medium-sized presence that curls affectionately at feet after field work without dominating small rooms. The bird-hunting heritage gives them a leggy, athletic frame suited to stamina rather than bulk.
answers.barking: English Setters do not bark a lot. Bred to crouch silently while setting on birds, they remain relatively quiet unless experiencing boredom or separation anxiety, at which point they may howl or vocalise to express loneliness. Their affectionate and gentle nature means the graceful hunter prefers leaning in for pets over raising an alarm. (PawLabs barking score: 4/10)
answers.apartment: No — English Setters do not suit apartment living well because their high exercise needs and boundless energy from bird-hunting days lead to restlessness and destructive behaviour when not given space to run. Although their affectionate temperament helps them settle indoors with family, the silky-coated hunter requires far more than short walks and can develop separation anxiety in confined routines.
answers.first-time: No — English Setters are not ideal as a first dog because their high exercise needs and tendency toward separation anxiety demand consistent time and commitment that can overwhelm novice owners. The intelligent and energetic bird hunter requires an owner who can channel its stamina and train its gentle yet mischievous side, or the affectionate breed will test patience with boredom-driven digging.
